title: Eval Gate Playbook for Structured-Output Changes
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Problem: Model and config changes (new checkpoints, quantization profiles, batching/kv-cache settings) occasionally introduce silent regressions in structured outputs (JSON-like contracts). Existing monitors surface token-level degradation but not schema-level correctness or field-level semantic drift. Goal: define a repeatable eval gate playbook that product, eng, and SRE can apply to any release path (hosted, dedicated, private) to prevent schema/regression rollouts without manual triage.

Scope: the playbook will cover: 1) a minimal standard set of schema adherence tests (syntactic + semantic field checks), 2) a gating threshold matrix (per-field fail rates, critical fields, fallback tolerances), 3) automated checks for PRs and canary releases, 4) dashboards/alerts in Console and runbooks for oncall, 5) post-rollout sampling and auto-rollback criteria. Not in scope: full retraining pipelines or human labelling workflows (those are upstream).

Deliverables: a one-page playbook (Confluence), a checklist for releases, integration spec for CI/GitHub status checks, ownership model for thresholds and runbooks, and a small initial eval suite (30–50 golden prompts + JSON schema tests) wired to the existing evals harness maintained by Research/Applied ML.
acceptance_criteria: Confluence playbook published with step-by-step gating flow and owner contacts
CI integration configured to block merges when gate thresholds are exceeded for structured-output changes
Console dashboard showing schema pass-rate, per-field error breakdown, and canary cohort metrics
Runbook and PagerDuty escalation defined for schema regression alerts
Automated rollback criteria documented and test-covered in canary pipeline
comments: 2026-03-06 - Maya Patel: Draft scope reviewed with Research and Serving runtime leads. Primary risk is flakiness from nondeterministic sampling; proposed mitigation is fixed seed prompt sets + diverse input generation.
2026-03-07 - Erik Sørensen (Research): Suggested adding semantic validators that check value constraints (enums, date formats, numeric ranges) in addition to JSON schema validation.
2026-03-08 - Priya Kapoor (SRE): Recommended linking alerts to canary percentage and adding a temporary 'soft-fail' mode for low-risk tiers to avoid blocking velocity.

2026-03-09 - Jasper Liu: Confirmed we'll reuse the existing eval harness repo (github.com/redwood-inference/evals-harness) and will add an initial 'schema-health' test runner. Opening ENG dependency tickets.
2026-03-10 - Design review (Ana Morales): UX for Console widgets sketched; request to include quick links from alert to example failing samples for faster triage.
risks_and_mitigations: False positives from heuristic validators could block healthy releases -> mitigate by using a two-tier threshold and allowing soft-fail auto-skip for low-severity fields
Large variance across models / quantizations -> mitigate by storing per-model baseline and requiring a minimum sample size before gating
Canary sample bias (not representative) -> mitigate by enforcing stratified sampling across top customer workload profiles
